newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BRIGHTON'S LATEST GROUND-SHARE BID TURNED DOWN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRIGHTON'S LATEST GROUND-SHARE BID TURNED DOWN.

text.p: Crisis-hit English soccer club Brighton have failed in their latest bid to find a temporary home.

The third division side, who have sold their Goldstone Ground and have to move next May, approached London club Fulham to discuss the possibility of ground-sharing until a proposed new stadium is built in Brighton.
But Fulham, also of the third division, said an agreement with their local council prevented them sharing.
"We are sympathetic to Brighton's problems but there's no question of anyone else but Fulham playing at Craven Cottage," club chairman Jimmy Hill said.
Brighton have recently been in discussion with south coast neighbours Portsmouth about sharing their Fratton Park ground, but Portsmouth have yet to make a decision.
In the meantime, Brighton, who played against Manchester United in the 1983 FA Cup final, are struggling on the pitch as well as off it.
They are currently bottom of the 92-team English Football League and their beleaguered board is under pressure to resign.
Brighton fans said they planned a mass walk-out 15 minutes before the end of Tuesday night's home match against Hereford in the latest in a series of protests against the way the club is being run.
